en.title: When does individual information improve PK/PD prediction?
en.summary: A reanalysis of warfarin PK/PCA data, revised with an absorption lag and a Hill exponent: effect delay, held-out prediction and the limits of extra PK.
key_findings: In 32 subjects with public single-dose warfarin PK and PCA data, a turnover model described the delay between concentration and response better than direct inhibition (held-out RMSE 0.0827 vs 0.0987 at the 24 h cutoff); version 1.1 added an absorption lag and version 1.2 a Hill exponent (1.28).
Adding each subject's PK measurements up to 24 or 48 h did not improve later PCA prediction: paired MSE differences were +0.0077 (0.0003 to 0.0174) and +0.0051 (−0.0013 to 0.0114), worse at 24 h.
The Hill exponent improved the in-sample fit but not held-out prediction. All current refits start from generic values; nothing here supports a dose, INR target or bleeding-risk claim.
